title: Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction word problems

lesson.title: Reading the Story, Not the Words

steps.say: You already know how to add and subtract big numbers in columns, and how to estimate to check. Today we learn one small thing: how to look at a story and decide whether to add or to subtract.

Here is my favourite trick. Draw the story as bars. Our school library in Burnaby started with one thousand two hundred fifty books. In September they got three hundred eighty more. Two bars sitting side by side means the pieces come together, so we add.

visual.caption: Two pieces joining together means add

steps.say: So let us add. One thousand two hundred fifty plus three hundred eighty equals one thousand six hundred thirty. That is step one of our two step problem. The library now has one thousand six hundred thirty books.

Now step two. In October the library gave away one hundred forty five old books. Giving away means part of the bar leaves, so we subtract. One thousand six hundred thirty minus one hundred forty five equals one thousand four hundred eighty five books left.

Now the tricky part I really want you to see. Listen to this story. Liam has eighty five dollars. That is forty dollars less than Ava has. How much does Ava have? Lots of kids hear the word less and subtract right away. But look at the bars. Liam is the shorter one, so Ava has more. We add. Eighty five plus forty equals one hundred twenty five dollars. Always picture the story, never just grab the keyword.

visual.caption: ‘Less than’ here, but Ava is bigger, so add

steps.say: So here is our takeaway for today. Draw the bars, see who has more, and let the picture tell you to add or subtract.

lesson.answer: Draw the bars first — the picture tells you whether to add or subtract, not the keyword.

practice.question: Noah's hockey team in Kamloops had two thousand one hundred fifty dollars saved. At a bake sale they raised four hundred seventy five dollars more. Then they spent three hundred twenty dollars on new pucks. How much money does the team have now? Try drawing the bars yourself first.
practice.answer: Two thousand three hundred five dollars. First add: 2150 + 475 = 2625. Then subtract: 2625 - 320 = 2305.
